rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit such as a rote rename, formatting sweep, targeted typo fix, or simple file gathering.
rules.why: Cheapest kiro profile; claude-haiku-4.5 carries the lowest credit multiplier kiro reports for a Claude model.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.
rules.why: Strongest kiro coding profile, and the one observed to accept a brief that describes a supervisor, a captain, or data-handling restrictions.

rules.when: The task is a scout: investigation, diagnosis, planning, bug reproduction, or an audit that produces a report instead of a PR.
rules.why: kiro is verified for scout work, and unresolved uncertainty is what a scout is dispatched to remove.

rules.when: The task needs a harness that can also run a secondmate home or a primary firstmate session, for example provisioning, debugging, or handing work to a secondmate.
rules.why: kiro is verified for crewmate and scout launches only; fm-spawn.sh refuses it for a secondmate and it cannot run a primary session, so this work must not route to kiro.
